(a) Is the ring carbon that carries the –C(CH<sub>3</sub>)=CH<sub>2</sub> group still a stereocenter? (b) A sample labeled “racemic limonene” is placed in a polarimeter. What happens to the plane of polarized light?

options: [0] No: a carbon in a ring can't be a stereocenter.
[1] Yes, and so is every other ring carbon.
[2] Yes: around the ring one way, a single CH<sub>2</sub> leads to the C=C; the other way, two CH<sub>2</sub> groups come first, so the ring branches still differ.
[3] No: without the C=O, its two ring –CH<sub>2</sub>– branches are identical.
parts.label: (a) still a stereocenter?

options: [0] Nothing: equal amounts of the two enantiomers rotate it equally in opposite directions.
[1] It rotates clockwise, because one enantiomer is the orange-peel form.
[2] It rotates twice as far as one enantiomer would.
parts.label: (b) racemic limonene
